Documentation → Automation & Change Control → Edit locks

Edit locks (lease locks)

A short, self-renewing lease that marks a configuration object as "being edited" in the object editor, so two people do not overwrite each other's changes — with a Take over button when the other editor walked away.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsprotection.edit network.edit
📍 WhereObject editor (full-page and inline edit of an existing object) (API /api/locks/…)

  • Edit an object

What is it?#

When you open an existing object in the object editor — full page or the inline editor embedded in configuration pages — SATOM takes a short lease on it — for example server-policy/policy:pol-shop on appliance fweb-01. While you keep the page open the lease is renewed every 30 seconds. A second user opening the same object sees that it is being edited and is blocked from saving until the lease expires or they take it over.

Edit locks are separate from the per-device write queue of jobs: the lease protects one object while somebody is editing it in the browser; the job queue serialises writes to the same appliance.

What does it do?#

  • Acquires a lease when an existing object is opened in the editor (not when creating a new object).
  • Renews it every 30 seconds; a lease not renewed for 120 seconds expires.
  • Shows other users a banner: "Being edited by . Saving is blocked to avoid a conflict." with a Take over button.
  • Refuses, on the server, a save or delete of the object while another user holds its lease.
  • Releases the lease when you leave the page or close the inline editor panel, and after a successful apply.
  • If your own lease is lost, shows "Your edit lock was lost (expired or taken). Reload before saving." with a Reload button.

Requirements#

  • A signed-in session with an edit permission (see below).
  • The appliance is one of the devices visible to you in the current console.
  • The object is opened in the object editor, full page or inline (for example the section configuration panel).

Permissions#

Acquiring, renewing and taking over a lease require any key that grants the legacy config_write — for example protection.edit, network.edit or operations.apply. A read-only user cannot take or take over a lease (they cannot save the object either). Releasing a lease and reading its status need only a signed-in session. Acquiring, taking over and reading the status of a lease work only on appliances visible to you (your visible devices in the current ADOM); a lease on any other appliance is refused. Saving the object still requires the editor's own permission (for example protection.edit or network.edit, depending on the object).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: taking, renewing and taking over a lease need an edit permission, edit leases are limited to your visible devices, the server refuses a save or delete while another user holds the lease, and the inline editor takes and shows the lease like the full-page editor.

How to use#

Edit an object#

  1. Open the object in the object editor. If nobody else holds it, no banner appears and you can edit normally.
  2. Save as usual. After a successful apply the lease is released.
  3. Closing or leaving the tab releases the lease (best effort); if the release is lost, the lease simply expires after 120 seconds.

When someone else is editing#

  1. The banner "Being edited by . Saving is blocked to avoid a conflict." appears and the Save actions answer "This object is locked by another user. Take over the lock first." A save or delete that reaches the server anyway is refused with "
